opening.welcome: You're about to paint a shaggy highland cow standing in tall golden grass at sunset, with violet hills and a glint of loch behind. What makes it sing is the cow's face: the pink nose peeking out of a long, glowing fringe, framed by two curved horns.
opening.light: The low sun sits behind the cow, near the horizon. It turns the sky gold where it sets, catches the edges of things, and wraps a bright gold rim round the cow's fringe and coat while its face and body stay in warm shadow.

skills.how: A nearly dry brush skimmed lightly so the paint breaks up on the canvas. It makes the cloud streaks, the shadowed hollows of the hills and the last glowing rim on the cow. Wipe the brush well: too much paint and it goes on solid.

Press the full width of the angle brush, then lift onto its edge as you pull, so each mark tapers to a point. Every hanging lock of the cow's coat is one of these. Lift at the end, or the locks look blunt and stuck on.

A quick upward stroke with the fan brush that lifts off as it goes, so each blade thins at its tip. It builds the tall grass in passes, darkest first. Keep the load light, or the blades turn into flat blobs.

opening.road: We start at the back: the sunset sky in one wet blend, then its clouds. The far hills and the loch go on next, then the green hillside, its bushes and the meadow, so the whole background is done fast. The first layers stop short where the next one covers them, so bare canvas showing early on is expected. Most of the time goes on the cow: a flat shape, shading, then two passes of hanging locks before the horns and the face. The tall grass is flicked over the cow's legs after, so it stands in the field. The brightest gold goes on last, when everything it covers is dry.

the-sky.for: The farthest thing first: a smooth sunset sky with soft cloud streaks across it.
the-sky.end: A blue-to-gold sky with orange and gold streaks lies across the canvas, and the rest of the canvas is still bare.

the-far-hills.for: Distance: pale and darker violet hills, shaded so they roll back, with a sliver of water at their foot.
the-far-hills.end: Two rolling violet ranges sit against the sky with a bright sliver of loch, and the rest of the canvas is still bare.

the-hillside-and-meadow.for: The ground the cow will stand on: a green hillside dotted with bushes and a glowing meadow base.
the-hillside-and-meadow.end: The whole canvas is covered: sky, violet hills, a bushy green hillside and a meadow glowing gold at its back and dark in front.

the-cows-shape.for: The cow as one big shape, then shaded so it starts to look round and shaggy.
the-cows-shape.end: A dark, shaggy rust cow stands in the meadow, with a lighter patch where its face will go.

the-shaggy-coat.for: The long hanging hair that makes it a highland cow.
the-shaggy-coat.end: The cow is covered in long copper locks with a few bright gold ones, and dark showing between them.

the-horns-and-face.for: The focal point: curved horns and a face that looks back at you.
the-horns-and-face.end: Two shaded horns curve up from the fringe, and a pink nose, nostrils, mouth and a shy eye give the cow its face.

the-tall-grass.for: Tall grass flicked over the cow's legs so it stands in the field, not on it.
the-tall-grass.end: Dark and olive blades with golden seed heads fill the meadow and rise over the cow's legs.

the-last-lights.for: The low sun's brightest touches, put on last over dry paint.
the-last-lights.end: The finished painting: a gold rim glows round the cow, the horns catch the light, and the meadow shines behind it.
